following

Order 
Present appeal under Section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is directed against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 26.06.2023 passed by learned I Additional Sessions Judge, District Guna (M.P.) in ST No.400055/2023 whereby, appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 420/120B of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for Seven years with fine of Rs.20,000/- with default stipulation.

sentences.text: During the course of appeal, it transpired that dispute between the parties has been amicably settled and application I.A.No.22684 of 2023 (jointly signed by both the parties) for permission to compromise in the matter has been moved by the complainant and appellant with their affidavits.
This Court vide order dated 21.12.2023, had directed the parties to appear before the Principal Registrar of this Court for verification of factum of compromise.
The Principal Registrar has submitted his report on 04.01.2024 and verified the factum of compromise.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that no act of cheating as alleged in the matter is proved against the appellant as defined under Section 420 of IPC.
As informed by him, appellant has suffered incarceration of more than Six months after passing of the impugned judgment on 26.06.2023 and remained in custody during pendency of trial also.
Therefore, indulgence is sought in the matter to quash the conviction recorded against the appellant.
Shri Sanjay Gupta, learned counsel for complainant, does not dispute about the compromise entered into between the parties.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Appellant stands convicted for offence punishable Under Section 420/120B of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for Seven years with fine of Rs.20,000/- with default stipulation.

It was proved that Deshraj in conspiracy with Vijay Shinde has proposed to sell House No.218 at Laxmiganj to Darshan Singh and fraudulently induced Darshan Singh to deliver money towards consideration of sell of aforesaid house, therefore, Deshraj stand convicted for offence punishable under Section 420 r/w Section 120-B of IPC.
Both the parties have requested that the incident relates to year 2011.

Dispute has become stale,
therefore, both the parties, who are closely acquainted with each other have decided to proceed with the life and amicably settled the dispute.
The offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC is compoundable, therefore, parties may be permitted to compound the offence.
Considering the nature of dispute, appellant's custody during trial and and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that parties may be permitted to settle their dispute.
The accused has not taken any undue advantage or acted against the law before or after the incident.
No criminal antecedent or past conviction is alleged against the appellant.
There is nothing on record that the compromise would have harmful effect on the social and moral fabric of the society.
It has no bearing on public order.
The parties at their own volition, without any coercion or compulsion wish to accord a quietus to the dispute.

The parties are well acquainted with each other, therefore,
amicable settlement of the criminal proceedings would advance peace and harmony between them.

Considering aforementioned aspects, this criminal appeal is disposed off with the following directions:-

sentences.text: The judgment of conviction and sentence dated 26.06.2023 passed by learned Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Distt. Guna in ST no. 400055/2011 against appellant Deshraj Jain for offence punishable under Section 420 r/w Section 120-B of IPC is set aside.
Consequently, appellant- Deshraj stands acquitted of offence punishable under Section 420/120B of IPC.
His personal bonds and surety bonds stand discharged.

(Narinder Singh v. State of Punjab, (2014) 6 SCC 466; Ram Gopal and Another Vs.
State of M.P. order dated 29.09.2021 in Criminal Appeal No.1489 of 2012 relied upon.)
